speaker_role: current admission counselors at University of Richmond (plus a student intern host)
key_insights: Write about what you can speak to best rather than what you guess the college wants; if it condenses to one sentence, the essay works.
To find a topic, spend a few timed minutes listing 15 to 20 ideas without editing; the later entries tend to be more distinctive.
If choosing between prompts, outline each option and see which best carries your authentic voice.
Reading celebrity or other memoirs can model how to write meaningfully about yourself.
Linking your writing to a specific program or professor shows you can picture yourself on campus.
Skip shock value; a genuine essay that reveals you as a person stands out more than a try-hard one.
Read the essay aloud to catch errors and confirm it sounds like you.
specific_numbers_or_facts: Brainstorm exercise: 5 minutes on the clock, 15 to 20 topics (one counselor).
notable_or_distinctive: Several different officers' tips in one place, but mostly standard advice.
reliability_notes: Brief panel format; advice is general and from one school's staff.
